extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germ ´an Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fem ´andez
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by extracting narrative passages from novels, specifically selecting those where human subjects can guess the last word given the full passage but not just the last sentence.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Narrative passages and full text extracted from novels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-step crowdsourcing protocol where subjects guess the missing target word. Step 1: one subject guesses based on the whole passage. Step 2: if correct, a second subject guesses based on the whole passage. Step 3: if correct, up to 10 subjects try to guess based on the target sentence only (up to 3 guesses each). Passages are kept if no subject in step 3 guesses correctly.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors used a strict hit-or-miss exact match approach for quality control, requiring perfect matches from two consecutive subjects for the broad context, and zero matches out of ten subjects for the local context, rather than evaluating synonymous continuations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 12 subjects per item (2 for the whole passage, and up to 10 for the target sentence only).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains a skewed Part-of-Speech (POS) distribution, where proper nouns are heavily over-represented and other categories (such as verbs, adjectives, and adverbs) are under-represented compared to the original input data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to be used as a benchmark for evaluating and testing computational language models, specifically assessing their ability to understand text and use broad discourse context for word prediction tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are hosted online for download, while the test set is planned for release in conjunction with a public competition.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was divided into development and test sets, ensuring that the passages were extracted from disjoint sets of novels to prevent data leakage. The training data was also kept disjoint from the dev and test sets.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: extracted from 1,331 and 1,332 disjoint novels, respectively

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The LAMBADA dataset consists of 10,022 passages, divided into 4,869 development and 5,153 test passages (extracted from 1,331 and 1,332 disjoint novels, respectively).

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: A random sample of the remaining passages were then evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in three steps. For a given passage, 1. one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... 2. a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We required two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word, and we made sure that no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only... For this reason we went for the strict hit-or-miss approach, keeping only items that can be unambiguously determined by human subjects.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: In fact, proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA, while the other categories are under-represented, compared to the POS distribution in the input.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The development set of LAMBADA, along with the training corpus, can be downloaded at http://clic.cimec.unitn.it/lambada/. The test set will be made available at the time of the competition.
